title: $F_X$ is flat over $E_X$
statement:
For finite extensions $E\le F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and every scheme $X$, the
extension of scalars $F_X\otimes_{E_X}-\colon\Mod_{E_X}\to\Mod_{F_X}$ along
$E_X\to F_X$ ([def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map], [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]) preserves
finite limits; that is, $F_X$ is flat over $E_X$.

proof.text: Choose a finite $E$-basis of $F$: a finite $\mathbf Q_\ell$-spanning list also spans over $E$, and a maximal independent sublist is a basis. By [lem-sfb-condensed-subfield-basis] it gives $\underline E^{\,n}\cong\underline F$ as internal $\underline E$-modules, with coordinate morphisms.

Put $P=p_X^*$. It is a strong monoidal left adjoint by [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. The left-adjoint colimit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] and [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] make $P$ additive. Both sheaf categories are abelian, so they have finite biproducts, and by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] each functor $A\otimes-$, $-\otimes A$ preserves colimits, hence is additive by [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive]; these are the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-monoidal-finite-free-transport], which we apply to the preceding basis. The transported rings and scalar map are precisely $E_X\to F_X$ by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]. Thus $F_X\cong E_X^{\,n}$ as $E_X$-modules.

The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies to the sheafified tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] on the chosen small pro-etale site. It preserves the underlying sheaf and section groups identically. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] supplies limits of internal $E_X$- and $F_X$-modules with sectionwise underlying groups. Restriction of scalars preserves these limits by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars].

Write $R=E_X$, $B=F_X$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates] to the basis of step 2. It gives $\operatorname{Res}(B\otimes_R M)\cong M^n$, naturally in $M$, with the stated inverse tensor coordinate maps.

For a finite diagram $D:J\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ with limit $L$, steps 3-4 identify the restricted canonical limit comparison with $L^n\to\lim_j(D_j^n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], on sections its inverse just reorders the indices of a compatible family $(x_{i,j})$; each arrow imposes the same coordinate equations. This includes the empty diagram, whose limit is zero. The comparison $a$ is $B$-linear and bijective on sections. Its inverse is $B$-linear since $a(b\,a^{-1}y)=b\,y=a(a^{-1}(by))$ and $a$ is injective. The sectionwise inverse commutes with restrictions by uniqueness. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism of internal $B$-modules under the equivalence of step 3, proving preservation of finite limits.
